name: Analyze any website's on-page SEO with AI and email the audit report

parameters.content:
## Analyze any website's on-page SEO with AI and email the audit report

### How it works

Paste a URL into a form and get a full on-page SEO audit in your inbox a minute later. The workflow fetches the page's real HTML, extracts the signals that matter — title tag, meta description, headings, image alt text, canonical URL and the readable copy — and also checks robots.txt for a declared sitemap.

Then it does something most AI auditors skip: **twelve deterministic checks run in plain code first** (title length, meta length, exactly-one-H1, word count, HTTPS, alt-text coverage, canonical, robots.txt, sitemap…), producing a baseline score out of 100 that can't be hallucinated. The AI writes the consultant-grade narrative on top of those verified numbers: what's good, what's broken, rewritten title and meta suggestions, and the five highest-impact quick wins.

The report lands as clean HTML email you can forward straight to a client, every audit is logged to a Google Sheets history, and if a site is down or blocks the request, the requester gets a polite failure notice instead of silence.

### Setup steps

Takes ≈10 minutes.

- Connect an OpenAI (or compatible) credential in **OpenAI GPT-4o Mini Model**.
- Connect your Gmail account in **Send Audit Report Email**, **Send Failure Notification** and — one click each on n8n Cloud — nothing else to configure there.
- Create a spreadsheet with columns `Date, Page URL, Score, Failed checks, Sent to` and select it in **Append Audit to Sheets Log**.
- Activate the workflow, open **When SEO Audit Requested** → *Test URL*, and submit a page with the email address the report should go to.

### Customization

- **Your own checklist:** the twelve checks live in one Code node (**Perform SEO Validations**) — add checks for Open Graph tags, structured data or your agency's framework; the score adapts automatically.
- **Audit depth:** edit the report structure in **AI Generates SEO Audit** — add Core Web Vitals notes, E-E-A-T, internal-link review.
- **Branding:** the report is markdown; add your agency header or a call-to-action line to the prompt and it appears in every report.
- **Lead magnet:** the form is shareable — every submission is captured with its email address in the history sheet.
- **Batch audits:** swap the form for a Google Sheets read of many URLs and loop; one report per row.

## Request an audit via form

Asks for the page URL and where to send the report. Shareable — works as a lead-magnet form on your site, and every request is captured in the history sheet.

## Fetch the page — fail loudly, not silently

Downloads the page's real HTML. If the site is down, private or blocking bots, the error output emails the requester a polite failure notice instead of dying without a trace.

## Extract signals and run 12 deterministic checks

Pulls the title, meta description, headings, image alt attributes, canonical URL and body copy, fetches robots.txt, then a Code node runs twelve pass/warn/fail checks and computes a baseline score out of 100 — real counts, not AI guesses.

## Grade the page with AI

The AI writes the consultant narrative on top of the verified check table: rewritten title and meta, heading and content review, and five prioritized quick wins. It is told to trust the table's numbers, not to re-count.

## Deliver the report and log the audit

Converts the markdown report to HTML, emails it to the address from the form, and appends URL, score and failed checks to a Google Sheets audit history.

You are a senior SEO consultant writing an on-page audit for a client. A deterministic check table and baseline score are provided — every claim about lengths, counts and technical facts must come from that table; never re-count them yourself. Write in markdown with these sections:

# On-Page SEO Audit — <domain>
**Overall score: N/100** — start from the provided baseline and adjust by at most ±10 for content quality; say in one line why you adjusted.

## Title & meta description
Grade click-worthiness and keyword placement; propose a rewritten title and meta description that respect the length checks.

## Heading structure
Use the H1/H2 facts from the table; comment on hierarchy and keywords in the actual headings.

## Content
Assess depth vs. thin content, search intent match, readability, obvious keyword gaps.

## Technical basics
One line each on HTTPS, canonical, image alt text, robots.txt and sitemap — verdicts from the table only.

## Quick wins
The 5 highest-impact fixes, ordered, each one actionable in under an hour.

Be specific to THIS page — quote its actual title and headings. No generic advice.
